caption: Fig. 1: The overview of CBAM . The module has two sequential sub-modules: channel and spatial . The intermediate feature map is adaptively refined through our module (CBAM) at every convolutional block of deep networks.
description:
## Convolutional Block Attention Module Overview
This figure illustrates the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), which consists of two sequential sub-modules: channel and spatial attention. The input feature is processed through the channel attention module, followed by the spatial attention module, resulting in a refined feature. The process is adaptive, refining the feature map at every convolutional block of deep networks.

## CBAM Components and Process
The figure shows the CBAM's components and process flow. It starts with an input feature, which is first passed through the channel attention module. The output of this module is then combined with the spatial attention module's output. The final refined feature is the result of these two attention mechanisms working in sequence.

caption: Fig. 2: Diagram of each attention sub-module. As illustrated, the channel sub-module utilizes both max-pooling outputs and average-pooling outputs with a shared network; the spatial sub-module utilizes similar two outputs that are pooled along the channel axis and forward them to a convolution layer.

It shows two sub-modules: the Channel Attention Module and the Spatial Attention Module. The Channel Attention Module uses max-pooling and average-pooling outputs with a shared network. The Spatial Attention Module uses similar outputs pooled along the channel axis, which are then processed by a convolution layer.

## Description
The figure contains two plots, each showing the Top-1 Error of different models over epochs. Plot (a) is for ResNet50 and plot (b) is for MobileNet. Each plot has six series, representing different training methods. The series with the highest Top-1 Error is ResNet50 Baseline train, and the lowest is ResNet50 + CBAM val.
